title: 2002 AMC 12B Problem 1
statement: The arithmetic mean of the nine numbers in the set \(\{9,\) \(99,\) \(999,\) \(9999,\) \(\ldots,\) \(999999999\}\) is a \(9\)-digit number \(M,\) all of whose digits are distinct. The number \(M\) does not contain the digit

solutions.text:
Each of the nine numbers is \(10^k-1,\) so their sum is \(9+99+\cdots+999{,}999{,}999.\) Dividing by \(9,\) \[ \begin{aligned} M &= 1+11+111+\cdots \\ &\quad {}+111{,}111{,}111 \\ &= 123{,}456{,}789. \end{aligned} \] Its digits are \(1\) through \(9,\) so the missing digit is \(0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Dividing each term by \(9\) turns the sum into \(1+11+111+\cdots\); add these and see which digit never appears
